name: William, Baron Craven to Prince Rupert, The Hague, 6 Nov 1648 (BL Add MS 18982 ff.134-135, DECODE R8447)
ciphertext_pending: No transcription in print (not in Warburton 1849) or as a DECODE attachment. DECODE R8447 has 3 pages, full images account-gated; BL images offline (searcharchives.bl.uk/catalog/040-002095608, 'digital images currently unavailable'). The BL note says the first part of the letter is heavily ciphered. Test 1 starts from a transcription.
alphabet: numerical (DECODE: Symbol Sets Numerical, Cipher Type Unknown)

constraints.tomokiyo: seems to use some different cipher from the volume's solved letters (unsolved.htm)
constraints.sibling_keys: same volume carries deciphered 1648 letters R8445 (f.114), R8446 (f.123), R8448 (f.141), R8449 (ff.146-147); no DECODE Key records for 18982
constraints.sender_recipient: Craven (Baron, later Earl) at the Hague to Rupert at Helvoetsluys, royalist fleet

cheap_tests_in_order: 1. Obtain the three pages (DECODE R8447 full-size via one browser login, record-specific; or BL if images return), transcribe by TRANSCRIPTION.md, count groups, value range, repeats. Cost ~$3.

2. Key-family test: apply the decipherments of R8445/R8446/R8448/R8449 (cipher values vs plaintext from the volume) as candidate tables to R8447, and the Cryptiana Nicholas-Rupert and THE=g4 keys, vs a shuffled-key control at the same N and symbol count (rule 3, match the design). Cost ~$3.
matched_control: shuffled-key control at the same N and K, same design (numeric code+nulls); to be run with test 2

judge.note: N unknown until test 1; 17th-century English, use an era-matched corpus if one exists in tools/data
